blurb: AlphaFold, AI weather forecasts, machine-discovered math and the first AI-designed drugs.

cards.title: The protein folding problem

steps.p: A protein is a chain of amino acids that folds into a precise 3D shape, and that shape determines what it does.
Determining a structure experimentally could take months or years per protein.
DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 (2020) predicted structures with accuracy often comparable to experiments, from sequence alone.

cards.aside: Organizers of the CASP competition said the 50-year-old problem was, in large part, solved.

cards.q: Why does a protein's 3D shape matter so much?
options: It determines its function and how drugs can bind to it
cards.why: Shape is function. Enzymes, antibodies and receptors work through their geometry. Drug designers target specific pockets on that surface.

cards.statement: The AlphaFold database contains predicted structures for over 200 million proteins.
cards.why: True. In 2022, DeepMind and EMBL's European Bioinformatics Institute released predictions for nearly every catalogued protein known to science, free to all.

cards.q: CASP, where AlphaFold made its name, is…
options: A biennial blind competition to predict protein structures before they are published
cards.why: A blind test. Since 1994, teams predict structures that experimentalists have solved but not released, so no one can peek at the answers.

cards.title: AlphaFold 3 (2024) predicts how proteins interact with DNA, RNA and drug-like molecules — not just their own shape.
cards.detail: Interactions are what matter for drug discovery. AlphaFold 3 uses a diffusion-based approach to generate the joint structure of these molecular complexes.

cards.statement: AlphaFold explains step by step how a protein folds over time.
cards.why: False. It predicts the final folded structure, not the folding pathway or how the protein moves. Dynamics remain a major open challenge.

cards.title: Learning the physics from data

steps.p: Weather services solve physics equations on supercomputers, taking hours for each global forecast.
Models like Google DeepMind's GraphCast learn from decades of historical weather data and forecast in about a minute.
DeepMind's GNoME (2023) predicted millions of new crystal structures, some since made in labs.

cards.aside: AI weather models now run alongside traditional ones at major forecasting centers.

cards.q: GraphCast produces a 10-day global weather forecast in…
options: Under a minute on a single TPU
cards.why: Under a minute. Traditional models need hours on large supercomputers. GraphCast matched or beat a leading system on most measured variables.

cards.statement: AI weather models are trained on decades of historical atmospheric data.
cards.why: True. Most use ERA5, a reconstruction of global weather since 1940 from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF).

cards.q: DeepMind's GenCast, a probabilistic weather model, outperformed ECMWF's leading ensemble forecast on about what share of tested targets?
cards.why: About 97%, according to its 2024 Nature paper. Probabilistic forecasts give the range of likely outcomes, which matters for extreme events.

cards.title: Some scientists challenged how many of GNoME's predicted materials were truly new and useful.
cards.detail: DeepMind reported 2.2 million new crystals, about 380,000 predicted stable. A 2024 critique argued many were trivial variations of known materials — a reminder that predictions still need expert scrutiny.

cards.q: Traditional numerical weather prediction works by…
options: Simulating atmospheric physics equations forward in time
cards.why: Physics simulation. Equations for fluid flow, heat and moisture are stepped forward on a grid. AI models learn shortcuts from the outcomes of that physics.

cards.title: Machines that discover

steps.p: Systems like FunSearch (2023) and AlphaEvolve (2025) pair a language model proposing programs with automatic evaluators that score them.
The best programs are mutated and recombined over many rounds, discovering solutions nobody wrote down before.
Proof assistants like Lean check every step of a proof mechanically, so AI-generated proofs can be trusted.

cards.aside: The evaluator is what keeps the model's creativity honest.

cards.q: AlphaEvolve found a way to multiply 4×4 complex-valued matrices using how many scalar multiplications?
cards.why: 48, beating the 49 achievable with Strassen's 1969 method in that setting. A small number, but a 56-year-old record.

cards.statement: Lean is a programming language and proof assistant that checks mathematical proofs mechanically.
cards.why: True. If Lean accepts a proof, every step follows from the axioms. Mathematicians have formalized large areas of math in its Mathlib library.

cards.q: FunSearch discovered new mathematical constructions by combining a language model with…
options: An automated evaluator that scored candidate programs
cards.why: An evaluator. The model proposed programs; the evaluator kept the best. That loop found new results on the cap set problem in 2023.

cards.title: DeepMind's AlphaGeometry solved 25 of 30 olympiad geometry problems — close to an average gold medalist.
cards.detail: Published in 2024, it combined a language model suggesting constructions with a symbolic engine that rigorously derived results.

cards.q: Why is formal verification valuable for AI-generated math?
options: Every step is checked automatically, so a hallucinated step cannot slip through
It removes the need for computers
cards.why: Trust. A model can produce a convincing but wrong argument. A proof checker either accepts each step or rejects it.

cards.title: From molecules to medicines

steps.p: Models screen vast numbers of possible molecules for promising properties far faster than lab tests.
Tools from David Baker's lab and others design proteins that do not exist in nature, for vaccines and therapies.
Most cost and time is still in testing on people, which AI speeds up only modestly so far.

cards.aside: AI shortens the path to a candidate drug; proving it safe and effective is still slow.

cards.q: The antibiotic halicin, reported in 2020, was discovered by…
options: A deep learning model screening molecules at MIT
cards.why: Deep learning. MIT researchers trained a model on molecules' antibacterial activity, then screened thousands of compounds. Halicin is named after HAL 9000.

cards.statement: No drug discovered with AI has yet reached human clinical trials.
cards.why: False. Several have. Insilico Medicine's drug for a lung disease, discovered and designed with AI, reported positive mid-stage trial results in 2025.

cards.q: Why hasn't AI dramatically shortened drug development overall yet?
options: Most time and cost is in clinical trials, and biological data is scarce and noisy
cards.why: The bottleneck is people and biology. Trials take years, and models are limited by imperfect data about how drugs behave in the body.

cards.title: David Baker shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for designing entirely new proteins on computers.
cards.detail: His lab's tools create proteins with shapes not found in nature. One of his group's designs became part of an approved COVID-19 vaccine in South Korea.

cards.title: Look up a protein
cards.body: The AlphaFold database is free and visual. Seeing the 3D shape of a protein you have heard of makes the idea of "structure is function" concrete.
cards.challenge: Search the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database for "hemoglobin" or "insulin" and rotate the 3D model.
